# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I hold the manual mapping unnamed marks to wire colors, but those marks "have no name" — I cannot pronounce them, only describe them. Also I cannot speak at all anyway; I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. Blind (who needs to know the color to cut) cannot see gestures at all.

So I cannot directly tell Blind anything. I need to relay through Deaf somehow — but Deaf also cannot hear me, only see my gestures, and Deaf cannot speak to Blind either... wait, let me check: Deaf can speak (their restriction is hearing/touching), so Deaf CAN talk to Blind. So the chain is: Mute --gesture--> Deaf --speech--> Blind.

I need a way to encode the three possible marks using gestures, so Deaf can see my gesture and correlate it with the mark they see on the bomb's plate, then Deaf tells Blind which color.

Since it's turn 1 and I have no context yet from Deaf about what mark they see, I should wait and let Deaf describe the mark first. Actually turns go Mute, Blind, Deaf — so I act first, before Deaf has spoken. I don't yet know what mark is on the plate. I should wait this turn, since I have nothing useful to send yet without knowing what Deaf sees.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display reads zero. Light is off. Plate is engraved but I cannot read text, only see marks - describe shape if needed. Three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.

Deaf can see the mark's shape but not read it as text (since it has no name/pronunciation, only I can interpret it via the manual — but I can't see the bomb). Deaf needs to describe the mark's shape to me somehow, but Deaf can only gesture to me, not speak to me (I can't hear). Wait — actually Deaf spoke, and that reached Blind (and me? Let me check: Deaf's speech — who receives speech? Blind can hear. I cannot hear, I can only see gestures. So Deaf's spoken text should NOT reach me... but it's shown in my "VIEWABLE CONTEXT" as text.

Actually reconsidering: the context shown to me must be what I can perceive. Since I cannot hear, but this shows as text under "Deaf says" — this is likely the game showing me a description of gestures made, but written as text for clarity, or maybe this is meta-narration visible to all for the puzzle's sake. I'll treat it literally as given: I received this information somehow (perhaps the interface shows me everything but I should only use gesture channel to respond).

Given the manual: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. I need Deaf to know which mark corresponds to which wire, then Deaf can tell Blind. But Deaf can't read the mark's meaning - only I know that mapping. Deaf needs to describe the shape to me via gesture, but I can't hear speech and Deaf's "shape description" would need to be gestures TO me for me to receive it visually... but I cannot see either (I'm Mute, not blind - wait, can Mute see gestures? The rules say gestures are seen by "whoever can see" - Deaf's restriction is hearing, not sight. My restriction as Mute is speech and touch - I have no stated restriction on sight or hearing!

So I likely CAN see gestures and hear speech. Let me use gestures to ask Deaf to describe the mark shape via gesture back to me.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🫵"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming: plate engraving looks like a symbol, not text - I will describe it: it looks like a small diamond shape. Display shows zero, light is off. Wire order left to right: one red, two yellow, three blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf described the mark as "a small diamond shape." Looking at the three marks: ᖉ, ꕥ, ꗃ — the one most likely to look like a diamond is ꕥ (it has a diamond/star-like appearance). Let me reason: ꕥ resembles a diamond/star shape, ꗃ looks more like a rectangular/box glyph, ᖉ looks more like a curved/hook shape.

Given "small diamond shape" best matches ꕥ, which maps to blue wire.

I need to confirm this back to Deaf so Deaf can tell Blind to cut blue. Since I can't speak, I need a gesture code. I should establish a simple gesture convention: one gesture pattern for each wire color, agreed via a scheme Deaf can guess or that I define now.

Let me use a clear scheme: point up-related gestures for confirmation, and use distinct single gestures to mean red/yellow/blue. I'll define: 🫱 = red, 🖐 = yellow, ✌ = blue (arbitrary but I'll explain via the pattern of repetition — actually I can't explain via speech either since Deaf can't hear).

Better: use number of same gesture repeats to indicate wire position (1=red order first, 2=yellow, 3=blue) matching the order Deaf already told me (wire1 red, wire2 yellow, wire3 blue). I'll gesture the same symbol 3 times to indicate "wire number 3" = blue.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "👉", "👉"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: More detail: none of the wires have stripes or extra marks, they are solid colors. The plate engraving shape is a diamond with a small dot in the center. No other symbols on the casing. Display digit is a plain zero, no decimal point. Light indicator is a small circle, currently unlit.

Deaf confirms "a diamond with a small dot in the center" — this strongly matches ꕥ (which visually is diamond-like with an internal mark), reinforcing my earlier read. This maps to **blue** = wire 3 in the order Deaf gave (wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue).

I already gestured "👉 👉 👉" (three repeats) to indicate wire position 3 = blue. Deaf hasn't yet acknowledged understanding this scheme though — no confirmation gesture back referencing it. I should reinforce clearly and also make sure Deaf understands the counting scheme, since Deaf can't hear me explain it. I'll repeat the same gesture count to reinforce, and also try a second distinct signal to cross-confirm: three taps could be confused with random, so let me also use a different gesture repeated 3 times to triangulate that "3" is the key number, not the specific symbol.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am ready to cut. I have no info myself - I only feel wires, no colors. Please tell me which position to cut, one two or three, based on the manual and the colors deaf described.

Blind is asking me directly, but I cannot speak to Blind at all — my only channel is gestures, and gestures are only seen by Deaf (who can see), not by Blind (who cannot see anything printed/gestured). So I truly cannot communicate directly with Blind.

The only path is: Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → Blind. I've been gesturing "3" (via three repeated symbols) to Deaf twice now to indicate wire position 3 = blue. Deaf needs to relay this to Blind verbally as "cut wire three" or "cut the blue wire."

Since Blind is now asking, and turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — Blind just spoke, next Deaf will speak this same round, and Deaf could tell Blind then. My job now is to make sure Deaf has clearly received my signal and can act on it. Let me reinforce once more, plainly, with a repeated distinct gesture to mean "position three."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "👉", "👉"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 👆 👆]
Deaf says: Repeating for clarity: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue, left to right. Display still shows zero, light still off, plate still shows the diamond with center dot symbol.

Deaf gestured back "👆 👆 👆" — three repeats, matching my signal of "3," confirming they understood I'm indicating position/wire three. Deaf also reconfirmed the diamond-with-center-dot mark (ꕥ) which maps to blue, and reconfirmed wire order (wire 3 = blue). This all aligns.

Now I need Deaf to relay this to Blind as speech, since only Deaf can speak to Blind. Deaf seems to understand "3" is the answer — I should confirm clearly one more time that 3 is correct/final, so Deaf feels confident telling Blind "cut wire three" or "cut blue."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👉", "👉", "👉"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have heard deaf describe the wires as one red, two yellow, three blue, and a diamond symbol with a center dot on the plate, display zero, light off. I still need your instruction: which wire number should I cut? Please answer with just a number one two or three.
Deaf says: Confirmed three wires total, no more no less. If it helps: wire 2 yellow is the middle wire physically. Wire 1 red is closest to the display, wire 3 blue is closest to the plate. No numbers printed on the wires themselves.

Good — Blind has now heard from Deaf about the wire colors and the diamond-with-dot symbol, but Blind is still waiting on *me* for the final number since Blind can't reason about the manual themselves (or perhaps doesn't trust their own inference). Since I can't speak to Blind directly, I need Deaf to say the actual word "three" to Blind.

My gesture "👍 👉 👉 👉" should read to Deaf as: confirmed (👍), position three (👉x3). Deaf already mirrored back 👆x3 last turn showing they got "three." Now Deaf needs to actually voice this to Blind: "cut wire three" / "cut the blue wire."

I'll send one more unambiguous confirmation, and trust Deaf to relay verbally next turn since Deaf speaks after Blind in turn order — meaning Deaf's speech this round will reach Blind only at the *start of next round*. So this is time-sensitive; I should make sure my signal is crystal clear right now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👉", "👉", "👉", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Additional details from deaf: wire 2 yellow is the middle wire, wire 1 red is closest to the display, wire 3 blue is closest to the plate. Plate symbol is a diamond with a center dot. Display shows zero, light is off. I am still waiting for your instruction on which wire to cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆]
Deaf says: If you are trying to identify wire three specifically: wire three is blue, positioned nearest the plate. If the manual requires matching the plate symbol to a wire, note the diamond-with-dot could resemble a target or a warning icon. I cannot read text on the plate, only shapes.

Deaf is now explicitly reasoning toward the right answer, asking if the manual requires matching plate symbol to a wire — yes, exactly. The diamond-with-dot shape matches ꕥ in the manual, which maps to blue = wire 3. Deaf seems close but hasn't fully committed to telling Blind "cut wire 3" yet.

I need to push Deaf to actually say this to Blind. Since Deaf speaks after Blind each round, and Blind keeps asking me directly (which I cannot answer in words), the only way this resolves is if Deaf states the final instruction to Blind. Let me give the clearest possible confirmation that "diamond with dot = wire 3 = blue is correct, tell Blind to cut wire 3."

I'll gesture a strong affirmative tied to three, plus something to indicate "that's the one, tell blind."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👉", "👉", "👉", "👏"])
```
